_note: Minor issues: local stories that turn up in the news for a few months. Any of them can be raised into a national debate, most easily while they are still in the headlines. 'when' makes a story likelier (x3) while the country is in that state. Lines: two per side (L = the axis's left side, R = its right). 'where': where the story happens; the game picks a province when it turns up: {"regions": [...]} (any province there; "city": true for provinces with a town only) or {"province": id}. Texts and lines write {city} (a town in that province, or the province's name if it has none), {province} and {region}.

ISSUES.title: A bridge falls in {city}
ISSUES.text: A road bridge in {city} fell into the river during the morning traffic. Nobody died, but it had been on a repair list for nine years.

L.text: Nine years on a repair list! {city} paid its taxes. Where did the money go?
My uncle drove over that bridge every day. Now he drives an hour around.

R.text: The money was there. The ministry spent it on itself. Audit them before you give them more.
The repair budget built three new ministry buildings in Cranebo.

ISSUES.title: Empty classrooms in {province}
ISSUES.text: A third of teaching posts in {province} are vacant. Some villages share one teacher between four grades.

L.text: Every child in Fauran deserves a teacher. Pay them properly to go where they are needed.
One teacher, four classes, a coal stove. That's a school in Fauran today.

R.text: Let Fauran's towns run their own schools and hire their own teachers. Cranebo has failed them.
The education ministry has more staff in Cranebo than there are teachers in Fauran.

ISSUES.title: The {city} plant closure
ISSUES.text: The steelworks in {city} will close in the spring. Twelve hundred jobs, and the owners are moving the machines to Dillihan.

L.text: They took the profits and now they take the machines. Nationalise the plant!
In {city}, everyone's father worked at that plant. Now everyone's son will leave.

R.text: {city} needs new businesses, and they come where taxes are low and rules are clear.
The plant closed because the unions priced it out of existence.

ISSUES.title: The {city} dockers' strike
ISSUES.text: Dockers in {city} have stopped work over pay. Ships are queueing outside the harbour and shop shelves in the west are thinning.

L.text: The dockers keep this country fed. Pay them like it!
A fair settlement now is cheaper than a long strike. The port owners should come back to the table.

R.text: The port must open. Shops are emptying and families are paying for a dispute they are not part of.
A handful of union bosses are holding the whole west of the country hostage!

ISSUES.title: Rents in {city}
ISSUES.text: Rents in {city} have doubled in three years. Young couples are moving back in with their parents.

L.text: Housing is a home before it is an investment. Cap the rents and build public flats.
My niece pays half her wage for one room in {city}. One room.

R.text: Rents fall when we build. Free up the land and the permits, and let builders build.
Rent caps are how you turn a housing shortage into a housing famine.

ISSUES.title: Dry wells around {city}
ISSUES.text: Wells around {city} are running dry for the second summer. Farmers are selling livestock they can no longer water.

L.text: {city}'s farmers fed this country. Now the country should help them through the drought.
When a farmer sells his cows to pay for water, the whole village knows it's bad.

R.text: Handouts end with the summer. {city} needs pipes and reservoirs, built by people who know the land.
Cranebo will send {city} a sympathy card and a committee.

ISSUES.title: Signs in {city}
ISSUES.text: The town council in {city} has put up street signs in Alinnian alongside {national}. The interior ministry wants them taken down.

L.text: One country, one official language. That is how a nation holds together.
Today it's the street signs. Tomorrow it's the border posts.

R.text: A street sign in two languages hurts nobody. Leave {city} alone.
If my grandmother can read the sign to the bakery, the country is stronger, not weaker.

ISSUES.title: The {city} checkpoints
ISSUES.text: Police checkpoints on every road into {city} have doubled travel times. Officials say they stopped two arms shipments.

L.text: If the checkpoints stop weapons, they stay. Safety comes first.
Two arms shipments stopped! The checkpoints are working!

R.text: A whole town treated as suspects is not security. Target the smugglers, not the commuters.
A nurse in {city} spends two hours a day showing her papers. She's not smuggling anything.

ISSUES.title: The Cranebo metro fares
ISSUES.text: Metro fares in the capital are going up by a third. Students have started jumping the barriers in groups.

L.text: Free transport for students and pensioners. The capital can afford it!
When the bus costs more than lunch, people stop going to work.

R.text: The metro loses money every year. Fix the management before asking anyone to pay more, or less.
Barrier-jumping students today, tax-dodging adults tomorrow.

ISSUES.title: The {city} hospital scandal
ISSUES.text: A report says the new hospital in {city} cost three times its budget and still has no working lifts.

L.text: We need the hospital and we need the truth. Finish it, then put the contractors on trial.
Patients carried up the stairs while contractors buy villas!

R.text: This is what happens when the state builds things. Three times the cost, half the result.
The only thing working in that hospital is the contractor's bank account.

ISSUES.title: The {city} festival
ISSUES.text: {city}'s summer festival is hosting its first pride parade. The mayor has received threats and a petition to cancel.

L.text: Every citizen has the right to march in their own town. The police should protect the parade.
{city} has always been a town where anyone could dance in the square.

R.text: A family festival should be for families. The town should keep it that way.
{city}'s grandparents built that festival. Nobody asked them.

ISSUES.title: The {city} grain subsidy
ISSUES.text: Big grain farms around {city} received most of last year's farm subsidies. Small farmers got almost nothing.

L.text: The subsidies went to the barons, not the farmers. Share them out!
The small farmer gets a letter, the big farmer gets a cheque.

R.text: Subsidies distort everything they touch. Phase them out and let farmers sell at a fair price.
{city}'s farm barons farm the ministry better than they farm the land.

ISSUES.title: Cameras in {city}
ISSUES.text: {city} wants face-recognition cameras on every street corner. Crime is down, the mayor says; so is privacy, say his critics.

L.text: If cameras keep {city} safe, other cities should follow.
My mother walks home at night again. I'll take the cameras.

R.text: A camera on every corner is a government in every home. {city} should stop now.
The mayor of {city} has a camera on everyone except himself.

ISSUES.title: Dillihan border stones
ISSUES.text: Dillihan surveyors have been setting border stones two kilometres inside Fauran. The border guard there has one working jeep.

L.text: They move the stones because they know we won't move them back. Send the army!
A country that can't guard its own border invites worse. Rebuild the border guard.

R.text: A border dispute is solved at a table, not with soldiers.
Farmers on both sides just want to know whose field it is. Let them talk first.

ISSUES.title: The mayor of {city}
ISSUES.text: The mayor of {city} hired his brother, his cousin and his tennis coach. He says they were the best candidates.

L.text: His brother, his cousin, his tennis coach! This is how the whole system works!
In {city} they don't have elections, they have family reunions.

R.text: One bad mayor is a case for the courts, not proof that democracy has failed.
Every town has a mayor like that once. The voters usually fix it.

ISSUES.title: The Arthemta reception centre
ISSUES.text: A reception centre for new arrivals is opening in Arthemta. Residents packed the town hall, half to protest and half to volunteer.

L.text: Arthemta was never asked. Decisions like this should be made with towns, not imposed on them.
Cranebo decides, Arthemta pays. Not anymore!

R.text: Half of Arthemta came to volunteer. That is the real story, and the government should back them.
Arthemta has always welcomed sailors from everywhere. It knows how.
